1.explanation: The Graticule class in src/ol/layer/Graticule.js is responsible for choosing angular intervals (getInterval_) and generating the grid and labels (createGraticule_, addMeridian_, addParallel_, drawLabels_, getMeridianPoint_, getParallelPoint_). Any slight floating-point imprecision in selecting the interval or the index arithmetic for label placement will propagate into the text positions. The default label formatter (degreesToStringHDMS in src/ol/coordinate.js) then converts decimal degrees into DMS, using Math.ceil on the seconds component, which can introduce off-by-one second values (e.g. 2.999″ → 3.00″ or 2.59″). Together these lead to labels that don’t line up on the exact uniform grid spacing, producing the strange 3′01″ or 2′59″ values.
1.bug_scenario: In the OpenLayers graticule example the grid lines are drawn at uniform pixel intervals, but the latitude/longitude labels at the top of the map appear at irregular angular intervals (e.g. 0°15′00″W, 0°12′00″W, 0°09′01″W, 0°06′00″W, 0°03′01″W, etc.), giving the impression of non-uniform spacing and odd second values (3′01″, 2′59″). The cells themselves are regular, so the mismatch points to how the labeling step and formatting are calculated and rounded.

2.explanation:
The core of the issue lives in the Graticule layer:
• getInterval_ picks a degree interval based on view resolution but can return non-integer minute/second values when converted to degrees.
• createGraticule_ (together with addMeridian_/addParallel_) uses that interval to lay out lines at those uneven steps.
Once those values reach the label formatter, degreesToStringHDMS in ol/coordinate.js uses Math.ceil and zero fractional-digit precision, which bumps seconds up irregularly (e.g. 0.016666…° → 1′ → 1″). Because getInterval_ and degreesToStringHDMS aren’t aligned to clean DMS boundaries, labels like “3′ .01″” or “2′ .59″” appear. Adjusting getInterval_ to choose round DMS intervals or tweaking degreesToStringHDMS rounding logic will restore consistent label spacing.
2.bug_scenario: In the Graticule example the grid lines themselves are drawn at regular pixel intervals but the latitude/longitude labels along the top show odd, non-round minute/second values (e.g. “0° 12′ 00″ W”, “0° 09′ 01″ W”, “0° 06′ 00″ W”, “0° 03′ 01″ W” etc.). In other words, the label formatter or interval calculation is producing irregular 3′.01″ or 2′.59″ offsets instead of clean multiples of minutes.
